personalInfo.name: Abdullah Saleh Robin
personalInfo.title: Senior Backend & Full-Stack Engineer
personalInfo.bio:
Senior Backend & Full-Stack Engineer with 9 years building enterprise applications in .NET with C# and in Java with Spring Boot, across e-commerce, healthcare, compliance and public-sector platforms.

I designed, built and ran an election-data platform end to end that processed 230,000+ scanned PDFs and 177M+ records, and served roughly 20M searches inside a 15-day national election window.

At Optimizely I co-engineered SpireWiz, cutting upgrade cycles by up to 80% and reclaiming 600+ developer hours a year. Microsoft Certified.
personalInfo.about: I have nine years of professional experience building scalable enterprise applications across e-commerce, compliance, healthcare and public-sector domains, working with distributed, cross-timezone teams across the US and Canada. My work centres on backend services, REST APIs and data-intensive systems, built in .NET with C# and in Java with Spring Boot, with Angular and React front-ends, together with applied AI: integrating LLMs into production systems with schema-constrained output and fallback handling. Based in Germany, available immediately, and authorized to work without sponsorship.

experience.description:
Identified the manual upgrade bottleneck and co-engineered SpireWiz, an AI-powered upgrade automation tool that applies the OpenAI Platform API to three-way merge analysis; automated 25+ annual upgrades, cut upgrade effort by around 80%, reclaimed 600+ developer hours a year, and contributed an estimated USD 180K in annual business impact.
Extended the Configured Commerce backend in C# through the platform's handler and pipeline extensibility model rather than forking it, including ERP integration pipelines to Infor CloudSuite Distribution and SX.e.
Pioneered the platform's first two Classic (Angular) to Spire (React) storefront migrations, delivered 55% faster than historical team averages, and codified the reusable migration playbook the team now applies to client upgrades.
Built OpalSpark, a .NET framework for Optimizely Opal AI tools with attribute-based tool discovery, configuration-driven authentication, health checks, rate limiting and request tracing, and shipped a tool on it exposing Configured Commerce order history.
Embedded AI-augmented delivery with Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and MCP-based tooling across B2B commerce projects; one custom DLL-to-extension migration went from a 200-hour estimate to 90 hours with human-reviewed code.
Reviewed 100+ pull requests across 15+ B2B client projects under a mandatory review process, mentoring developers and cutting deployment errors.

Built the real-time layer of an NFT and digital-asset marketplace on .NET with SignalR and Socket.IO, holding connection state in Azure Table Storage rather than Redis or memory so live sessions survived restarts and scale-out.
Secured the real-time transport with dual authentication: JWT for browser clients and HMAC-SHA256 signed tokens for socket clients that cannot send headers.
Targeted broadcasts through persisted page flags instead of SignalR group lifecycle management, with stale-connection cleanup under optimistic concurrency; containerized development and deployment with Docker.

Led 8-10 engineers across government digital transformation, healthcare, telemedicine and commerce automation projects.
Architected and built the service layer behind a national skills-certification platform used by 100,000+ training providers, assessment centres and skilled workers, with JWT authentication, role-based access control, SMS one-time-password verification and a national payment-gateway integration.
Engineered the APIs behind the national telemedicine contact centre serving 30M+ rural residents, with PBX events fanned out through RabbitMQ to WebSocket dashboards; the centre handled 100,000+ teleconference calls a day.
Built a multi-tenant Facebook page automation platform across four services, sustaining 800 concurrent messages per second across 50+ pages, with Rasa NLP intent handling and in-chat product discovery and checkout.
Deployed and operated a microservice fleet for the national device-identity register (API gateway, service discovery, inter-service clients, circuit breaking, Kafka messaging) with rolling releases and rollback.
Built a COVID-19 telehealth CRM with a runtime questionnaire builder that let operators change patient-intake questions without a code change; it supported care for 10,000+ patients daily.

Built full-stack public-sector and healthcare systems, backend services and Angular front-ends.
Started several platforms from scratch and set the project structure and coding conventions the team worked in afterwards.
Delivered the e-prescription service, a shared microservice sending prescriptions to patients by SMS across several national healthcare platforms, averaging 50,000 prescriptions a day, with a configuration-driven gateway that let new SMS vendors be added without a backend code change.
Reduced report-generation query latency by around 70% through targeted database indexing.
Owned root-cause analysis for critical production incidents.

education.description: CGPA 3.41 out of 4.00. Focused on software engineering principles and web development, with coding competitions alongside coursework.

projects.title: Optimizely Configured Commerce
projects.description: Enterprise B2B commerce delivery on Optimizely Configured Commerce across 15+ client projects, covering Spire (React) and Classic (Angular) storefronts, custom handlers, ERP integrations and the upgrade path between platform versions. Co-engineered SpireWiz, which cut upgrade effort by around 80% and returned 600+ developer hours a year, delivered the platform’s first Classic-to-Spire storefront migrations, and built OpalSpark, a .NET framework for Optimizely Opal AI tools, plus a proof-of-concept Opal to Sitecore integration. Reviewed 100+ pull requests across the client portfolio.

projects.title: Parsing Project
projects.description: Election-data processing platform for 340+ client organisations in Bangladesh, in production 2021 to January 2026. I designed, built and operated it: an OCR and LLM document pipeline over a 65M-record PostgreSQL database, served by two Angular SPAs on Kubernetes. It processed 230,000+ scanned PDFs and 177M+ voter entries, and served roughly 20M searches during a 15-day national-election window.

projects.title: National Skills Authority (NSDA)
projects.description: Bangladesh’s national skills-certification platform, used by more than 100,000 skill-training providers, assessment centres and skilled workers. Architected the modular, service-based backend with an access-control layer, two-factor authentication and payment-gateway integration, and built the Angular interface including secure 2FA payment journeys and dynamic certificate issuance. Led the developer team and automated database backup to a secured off-site location.

projects.title: Shastho Batayon (16263)
projects.description: Bangladesh’s national telemedicine contact centre, serving remote diagnosis over teleconference to more than 30 million rural residents and handling 100,000+ teleconference calls a day. Built the real-time telephony layer, with Asterisk PBX events fanned out through RabbitMQ to STOMP WebSocket dashboards and consumers scaling elastically from 4 to 16 under load, plus a visual IVR builder and the doctor routing that let clinicians join and leave the call queue on demand. The same platform was later deployed for Telenor Health.

projects.title: National Equipment Identity Register
projects.description: Bangladesh’s national device-identity register (BTRC), built as a scalable Spring Cloud microservice system. Served as the deployment and operations engineer, writing bash automation covering 11 microservices and used to roll out around 40 redundant service instances across nodes, where deployment had previously been manual and error-prone. Contributed performance and defect-fix work across the service fleet.

projects.title: Shastho Batayon Corona Bot
projects.description: A Facebook Messenger bot on the official 16263 national health hotline page, giving the public COVID-19 self-assessment and daily statistics through the pandemic. Guided symptom self-assessment in chat let people check themselves without occupying a hotline operator at peak demand, and the resulting assessment statistics were used by the health authorities. Built on the Node.js page-automation base from Trendy Bot, re-purposed for public health.

projects.title: Covid-19 Patient Management
projects.description: Telehealth CRM for triaging suspected COVID-19 patients, used by trained doctors for remote consultation. Designed a runtime questionnaire builder in Angular so operators could add, edit and reorder patient-intake questions without a code change, and built the report-generation layer for administrators. Supported care for 10,000+ patients daily during the pandemic.

projects.title: E-Prescription Service (gRPC Microservice)
projects.description: A shared Spring Boot microservice delivering e-prescriptions to patients by SMS, used across several national healthcare platforms and sending around 50,000 prescriptions a day. New SMS vendors were added through configuration alone, with no backend code change. Delivery adapted to the handset: smartphones received one message, feature phones received ordered parts.

projects.title: Trendy Bot (Multi-Tenant Facebook Commerce Platform)
projects.description: A multi-tenant platform automating Facebook pages for commerce, built on .NET across four services with a Node.js edge for the Messenger integration. Served more than 50 pages from a single deployment, sustaining 800 concurrent messages per second, with per-tenant configuration, scheduled broadcast campaigns and in-chat checkout.

projects.title: Shared File Service (gRPC Microservice)
projects.description: A shared microservice handling file upload and download for other services, consumed independently by two national platforms. Callable over gRPC, storing small to large files concurrently on server storage, deployed on premises.

projects.title: Telenor Health
projects.description: A second deployment of the national telemedicine platform for a separate commercial venture, running the same core codebase with client-specific tuning. This is what proved the contact-centre platform was a reusable product rather than one bespoke build.

projects.title: Point of Sale (Open Source)
projects.description: An ASP.NET MVC point-of-sale web application covering products, barcodes, suppliers, purchases, sales and printed receipts. Published open source and picked up by other developers as a reference implementation. An earlier desktop version was built in WPF on a three-layer separation with LINQ to SQL and Crystal Reports.

projects.title: Makkah Hotel Management System
projects.description: Multi-tenant hotel management and booking platform, designed and built end to end. Tenant isolation runs across four independent layers: HTTP middleware, Entity Framework Core global query filters on reads, a SaveChanges interceptor on writes, and PostgreSQL row-level security on the tables themselves. Onion architecture with domain-driven design, and a Next.js front end in strict TypeScript with right-to-left Arabic support.

projects.title: Digital-Asset Platform (Real-Time Layer)
projects.description: Real-time layer of an NFT and digital-asset marketplace, built for a US client on .NET with SignalR and Socket.IO. Connection state lives in Azure Table Storage rather than Redis or memory, so live sessions survive restarts and scale-out; the transport is secured with JWT for browsers and HMAC-SHA256 signed tokens for socket clients, and broadcasts are targeted through persisted page flags instead of SignalR group lifecycle management.

projects.title: SpireWiz
projects.description: AI-powered upgrade-automation tool for Optimizely Configured Commerce. Every client blueprint upgrade meant resolving three-way merge conflicts by hand between the client’s customisations, their old platform version and the new one. SpireWiz puts the OpenAI Platform API into that merge analysis, classifying each conflict and proposing a resolution for a developer to review before it lands. Automated 25+ annual upgrade workflows, cut upgrade effort by around 80% and reclaimed 600+ developer hours a year, an estimated USD 180K in annual business impact.

projects.title: Probash Bondhu
projects.description: A call-centre CRM supporting Bangladeshi immigrants abroad with immigration and general medical problems. Appointment scheduling matched users with doctors who were themselves immigrants, so callers spoke to someone who had been through the same process. 40 doctors served on the platform, supporting more than 30,000 immigrants.

featured.title: SpireWiz
featured.tagline: AI-powered upgrade automation for Optimizely Configured Commerce.
featured.description: Optimizely Configured Commerce upgrades were a manual, repetitive drag on every client project. We put the OpenAI Platform API into three-way merge conflict analysis so the tool proposes resolutions instead of engineers hand-reconciling each one, and folded it into the delivery workflow across enterprise B2B projects.

featured.title: Parsing Project
featured.tagline: Election-data processing platform for 340+ client organisations in Bangladesh.
featured.description: In production from 2021 to January 2026. An OCR and LLM document pipeline over a 65M-record PostgreSQL database, served by two Angular SPAs on Kubernetes. The heavy compute was deliberately pushed to background workers and the browser so the API stayed a thin store-and-serve layer, which is what let it hold up through a national election.
